name: Haven
_comment_storage: ENG-2198: declaring managed_schema is what makes chrome.storage.managed exist at all. Without this key the namespace reads as permanently empty and a deployment token in enterprise policy is silently ignored — no error, just an extension that never enrolls anyone.
_comment_web_accessible_resources: ENG-3196: there are NONE, deliberately. This listed mascot-facing-left.png, icon-egg.svg, icon-egg-white.svg and icons/* against <all_urls>; only icon-egg-white.svg ever had a page consumer (the in-page and Gmail banners), and those now draw the Haven mark as inline SVG (lib/haven-egg-mark.ts) so the page's own CSP cannot strip Haven's mark off its own warning. Anything listed here is fetchable by ANY site, and because this extension pins a fixed `key` the ids are stable, so every entry is a reliable way for a page to detect Haven. Do not re-add one to ship an image: inline it. If an entry ever is genuinely required, add `"use_dynamic_url": true` so the URL is not a stable probe. Note `_favicon/*` in particular must never go here — it would let any page test which sites are in the user's favicon cache (see lib/protected-tabs.ts).
_comment_externally_connectable: ENG-2730: PRODUCTION trusts the account site and nothing else. The alpha auth host used to be listed here too, which let anything served from alpha drive auth-complete on the production extension and sign it into an arbitrary account. Alpha ships in manifest.canary.json, which build-canary.sh Object.assigns over this whole key.
